{{short description|American chemist and molecular biologist}}
'''Helen E. Blackwell''' (born 1972)<ref name="iota">{{cite web|title=2009 IOTA SIGMA PI AGNES FAY MORGAN RESEARCH AWARD|url=http://www.iotasigmapi.info/awards/agnesfaymorgan/2009.pdf|accessdate=26 October 2017}}</ref> is an American organic chemist and chemical biologist. She is a professor at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]].

==Education==
Blackwell is a native of Shaker Heights, Ohio and was educated as an undergraduate at [[Oberlin College]], receiving a Bachelor of Arts degree in chemistry in 1994. She received a Ph.D. in organic chemistry from the [[California Institute of Technology]] in 1999 working with [[Robert H. Grubbs|Robert Grubbs]].<ref name="iota"/><ref name="chemwisc">{{cite web|title=blackwel {{pipe}} UW-Madison Department of Chemistry|url=https://www.chem.wisc.edu/users/blackwel|accessdate=26 October 2017}}</ref><ref name="thescientist">{{cite news|last1=Perkel|first1=Jeffrey M.|title=SCIENTIST TO WATCH {{pipe}} The Scientist Magazine|url=http://www.the-scientist.com/?articles.view/articleNo/24043/title/SCIENTIST-TO-WATCH/|accessdate=26 October 2017}}</ref>

==Career and research==
Nearing the end of her doctoral education in 1999, Blackwell gained an interest in biology and joined [[Stuart Schreiber]]'s lab at [[Harvard University]]. At the time, the lab was focusing on animal models, but Blackwell decided to work with plants. During her research, Blackwell identified several small-molecule [[sirtuin]] inhibitors in ''[[Arabidopsis]]'' plants.<ref name="thescientist"/>

Blackwell's research utilizes [[chemical probe]]s—synthesized using solution-phase and solid-phase synthesis, and [[combinatorial chemistry]]—to better understand bacterial communication and interactions between a microbe and its host, more specifically, how plants and animals react to microbe invasion,<ref>{{cite news|last1=Helen E.|first1=Blackwell|title=Bacteria talk to each other, and we're listening|url=http://host.madison.com/wsj/discovery/bacteria-talk-to-each-other-and-we-re-listening/article_03ae7a11-72f6-5a7c-a4bd-0c3ca6e7dedd.html|accessdate=26 October 2017|work=Wisconsin State Journal}}</ref> and how bacteria use [[quorum sensing]] to determine when to attack their host.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Iacurci|first1=Jenna|title=Bacteria Know When to Turn Deadly|url=http://www.natureworldnews.com/articles/9133/20140920/bacteria-know-when-to-turn-deadly.htm|accessdate=26 October 2017|work=Nature World News}}</ref><ref name="chemwisc"/>

Blackwell is a [[fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science]],<ref>{{cite web|title=AAAS Members Elected as Fellows|url=https://www.aaas.org/news/2011/01/11/aaas-members-elected-fellows|accessdate=26 October 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180913040407/https://www.aaas.org/news/2011/01/11/aaas-members-elected-fellows|archive-date=13 September 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> and has received the [[Agnes Fay Morgan Research Award]].<ref name="iota"/>

==Publications==
Blackwell has written more than 130 academic journal papers, she is the co-author of {{cite journal|title=Identification of a Class of Small Molecule Inhibitors of the Sirtuin Family of NAD-dependent Deacetylases by Phenotypic Screening|journal=[[The Journal of Biological Chemistry]]}}, {{cite journal|title=New Approaches to Olefin Cross-Metathesis|journal=[[Journal of the American Chemical Society]]|year=2000|doi=10.1021/ja993063u|last1=Blackwell|first1=Helen E.|last2=O'Leary|first2=Daniel J.|last3=Chatterjee|first3=Arnab K.|last4=Washenfelder|first4=Rebecca A.|author4-link=Rebecca Washenfelder|last5=Bussmann|first5=D. Andrew|last6=Grubbs|first6=Robert H.|volume=122|issue=1 |pages=58–71|bibcode=2000JAChS.122...58B |url=https://resolver.caltech.edu/CaltechAUTHORS:20170516-131732124 }}, and {{cite journal|title=Small Molecule Inhibitors of Bacterial Quorum Sensing and Biofilm Formation|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|doi=10.1021/ja0530321 | volume=127|year=2005|pages=12762–12763 | last1 = Geske | first1 = Grant D. | last2 = Wezeman | first2 = Rachel J. | last3 = Siegel | first3 = Adam P. | last4 = Blackwell | first4 = Helen E.|issue=37|pmid=16159245|bibcode=2005JAChS.12712762G }}<ref>{{cite web|title=Microsoft Academic|url=https://academic.microsoft.com/#/detail/2460979789|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160316140810/https://academic.microsoft.com/#/detail/2460979789|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 16, 2016|publisher=[[Microsoft Academic Search]]|accessdate=26 October 2017}}</ref>
